issue.title: GraalVM 22.3.0-dev Quarkus native readiness tracker

repository.name: mandrel
repository.description: Mandrel is a downstream distribution of the GraalVM community edition. Mandrel's main goal is to provide a native-image release specifically to support Quarkus.

issue.body:
We are seeing some CI failures in quarkus native integration tests on the master branch (22.3.0-dev tree). This serves as a tracker for all issues in prep for the 22.3.0 release:

# Mandrel only (not seen with GraalVM CE):

https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/27211 (Fixed with https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/27225)

# GraalVM CE and Mandrel:

https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/27232 (Fixed with https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/27366)
https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/27300 (Fixed with https://github.com/oracle/graal/pull/4997)
https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/27791 (Fixed with https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/27960)

body:
Hi @jerboaa, thanks for the report - this is going to be interesting :)

I've created this test myself, to verify some assumptions we have on how GraalVM's dead code elimination could be "guided" and enable stronger optimisations.

This implies that such a regression isn't critical in terms of functionality: the application will behave the same semantically; but it might be a performance regression - how far I don't know yet.

Essentially with this particualr integration test I was expecting us to be able to avoid needing to include the XML parser code within the native-image; there's some tricky code in the Hibernate ORM (JPA) extension that was supposed to "help" the GraalVM compiler to come to this conclusion - either this is no longer effective (changes on the compiler side?) or some other component in Quarkus has inadvertently lead to including the XML parser on its reachability graph.

However  since this only failed in GraalVM 23.3.0-dev (and not in the current one we use for integration testing), I suspect it's more likely to be due to a change in GraalVM than a change in Quarkus - otherwise we'd have seen the test fail earlier.

Admittedly the things we did in Quarkus to avoid including the parser were rather "fragile"; that's why I added this test, so to spot such cases quickly.

Do you know the range of commits in GraalVM at which it started failing?
BTW the optimisation was crafted using @galderz 's scripts to analyze the reachability graph using neo4j

@Sanne Note that I didn't reproduce with a GraalVM CE dev build (used the same one) with quarkus at revision `4f53bdd6f377edcc783e3a91b3ea3e24794cfc81`, I'm not 100% sold on it being a graal issue. Does anything between `4f53bdd6f377edcc783e3a91b3ea3e24794cfc81` and `bc451819b26ba4a084349ebdac3532e732b618ae` stand out to you that could have caused this?

> Admittedly the things we did in Quarkus to avoid including the parser were rather "fragile"; that's why I added this test, so to spot such cases quickly.

Could you please point me to those changes?

> Do you know the range of commits in GraalVM at which it started failing?

I'll see if I can find out. It's definitely quarkus related as well.

As reference, one needs to understand the different expectations in these two tests:
 - https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/af8b95d75ab9c8e77cfb90b4ab9aff867eae2eec/integration-tests/jpa-postgresql-withxml/src/test/java/io/quarkus/it/jpa/postgresql/JPAFunctionalityInGraalITCase.java
 - https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/af8b95d75ab9c8e77cfb90b4ab9aff867eae2eec/integration-tests/jpa-postgresql/src/test/java/io/quarkus/it/jpa/postgresql/JPAFunctionalityInGraalITCase.java

N.B. these are similar tests (with same name) but located in different modules. The first one does use XML, the second does not.

This GraalVM Feature works as a "toggle", enabling support for XML in the postgresql JDBC driver if (and only if) those types are also reachable via other means:
 - https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/57fb6526814cd66b92a4f3d40c9f638a7133a12a/extensions/jdbc/jdbc-postgresql/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/jdbc/postgresql/runtime/graal/SQLXMLFeature.java

Finally, the substitutions in `io.quarkus.jdbc.postgresql.runtime.graal.PgSQLXML` apply as well

@Sanne So it looks like it's caused by this commit: https://github.com/oracle/graal/commit/89fdc4232159852300e11d2952cd1932b77b7b9a

If I had to guess, move of `NeverInline` annotation might be the issue? If that's the case adding `-H:NeverInline=<string>*` to the native image build might fix it.

@jerboaa thanks for finding it!

So it might be because of package changes like these?

https://github.com/oracle/graal/commit/89fdc4232159852300e11d2952cd1932b77b7b9a#diff-947ac1347c188508d95be452d074199eb5f11565d29403f98f8fd3ca1617b67bL43-R45

I don't mind if this particular optimisation is broken temporarily (we could even disable the test for a while), but I'm concerned if such changes could break any other optimisation.

As far as I know, we have very limited testing about such needs being effectively applied (this being one of them - perhaps the only test)

Considering the current `svm` artifact is being deprecated - but not removed - I would have expected the existing annotations to still be effective, or fail/warn in some way.
